name: Myxopapillary Ependymoma
aliases: Myxopapillary Ependymoma of the Filum Terminale

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Histopathological identification of myxopapillary architecture with papillary structures and myxoid stroma
MRI demonstrating a well-circumscribed, enhancing mass in the filum terminale or conus medullaris region
Positive GFAP and S-100 protein immunostaining supporting ependymal origin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of myxopapillary architecture with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing is not routinely required but may assist in difficult cases.

common.symptomName: Neoplasm of the central nervous system

imaging: MRI showing well-demarcated, enhancing mass at filum terminale or conus medullaris
T1-weighted images: iso- to hypointense lesion
T2-weighted images: hyperintense lesion with possible cystic components
genetic: No recurrent genetic mutations identified; molecular profiling not routinely diagnostic
other: Histopathology reveals papillary structures with myxoid stroma and ependymal cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for GFAP and S-100 protein

distinguishingFeatures: Classic ependymomas occur throughout the CNS and lack myxopapillary architecture
Different anatomical location and histopathological features
Schwannomas arise from nerve sheath cells and show Antoni A and B areas histologically
Typically S-100 positive but lack papillary myxoid features
Astrocytomas show GFAP positivity but lack papillary and myxoid histology

redFlags: Severe, unremitting radicular pain refractory to analgesics
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Kleihues P, Cavenee WK. Pathology and Genetics of Tumors of the Nervous System. IARC Press, 2000.
